channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Tunis Pasteur Institute amphitheatre rehabilitation begins
item.description: The historic science venue will receive a new design and modern equipment while preserving its architectural identity.

item.title: Female artisanal miners report systemic sexual violence in Kono district
item.description: Women working in abandoned diamond and gold pits in Jaiama Nimikor describe a pattern of rape and harassment with little recourse from local authorities.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning causes deforestation
item.description: The practice of burning wood for charcoal is depleting forests and threatening food security, according to environmental officials.

item.title: Sierra Leone vice presidents face succession challenges
item.description: The office has historically served as a political cul-de-sac, with no vice president ever elected president.

item.title: Finance minister's defenders say calls for his sacking are misplaced
item.description: A Politico SL guest column argues that a civil society group's demand to remove Sheku Ahmed Fantamadi Bangura confuses global shocks with local mismanagement.

item.title: Namibia's chief vet rallies //Kharas leaders on FMD
item.description: Dr Kennedy Shoombe toured the region to assess containment strategies and boost veterinary teams battling the outbreak.

item.title: Mauritius inflation climbs to 6.4% in October
item.description: Annual inflation in Mauritius accelerated to 6.4% in October 2026, up from 5.7% in September, driven by fuel price adjustments.

item.title: Port-Louis traffic rerouted around Mgr Leen street construction
item.description: New traffic plan in Port-Louis aims to ease congestion near ongoing infrastructure work on Mgr Leen street.

item.title: Togo president attends Francophonie summit in Cambodia
item.description: Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé joined other leaders in Phnom Penh for the 20th Francophonie Summit, focusing on peace and dialogue.

item.title: Mombasa teacher assault not linked to KCSE, says CS
item.description: Education CS Julius Ogamba stated the attack on examination supervisor Julius Ndurya was due to personal issues, not exam malpractice.

item.title: Mali's foreign minister Abdoulaye Diop, a career diplomat, backs the military transition
item.description: Diop has served under Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta and Assimi Goïta, moving through political changes without leaving the centre of power.

item.title: NOCAL breaks ground on Sinje hospital trauma ward
item.description: The National Oil Company of Liberia is building a trauma ward at Sinje Hospital, due to be finished and dedicated within 16 months.

item.title: Lawyer Lonias Majoni asks Parliament to probe Zimbabwe football governance
item.description: Majoni's complaint to the football association and the Premier Soccer League went unanswered after a seven-day deadline lapsed.

item.title: Ex-Liberia minister jailed for rice diversion
item.description: Former Foreign Minister Dee-Maxwell Saah Kemayah sentenced to 10 years for diverting 25,000 bags of Saudi rice meant for flood victims.

item.title: Namibia urges UN to back Western Sahara's self-determination
item.description: Ambassador Penda Naanda asked the Security Council to restart talks aimed at a peaceful settlement of the dispute.

item.title: Nine shot dead in Atteridgeville shack
item.description: Police are hunting gunmen after six men and three women were found with gunshot wounds in Jeffsville informal settlement on Monday morning.

item.title: Senegal wins right to host 2031 Francophonie Games
item.description: The Permanent Council of La Francophonie picked Senegal on 13 October 2026, a first for the country, after Dakar hosted the Youth Olympic Games.

item.title: US senator demands report on Liberia's human rights record over deportation deal
item.description: Senator Tim Kaine filed a resolution asking the US State Department for a formal statement on Liberia's treatment of deportees.

item.title: CDC accuses government of selective justice in Jackson case
item.description: The opposition party demands economist Samuel P. Jackson receive medical treatment abroad, citing alleged double standards.

item.title: Liberia's diplomats press Washington for a second U.S. grant
item.description: Liberia has been trying to win a second five-year Millennium Challenge Corporation compact for nearly a decade, and the agency is now smaller and less certain about its future.

item.title: Sudan and Ethiopia trade accusations over armed groups
item.description: Sudan's military and Ethiopia each accuse the other of harbouring armed groups that fight inside their borders, and each denies the charges.

item.title: Senegal's Lions need one win to edge closer to CAN 2027
item.description: Senegal, leaders of Group J with 7 points, face Sudan in Juba on Monday, needing a win and a Mozambique loss to Ethiopia to qualify directly.

item.title: Mali ministers promise accountability on state TV
item.description: Government officials defended their departments' actions in special broadcasts from November 9 to 14, but questions remain about the gap between official figures and daily life.

item.title: Mozambique used car prices rise again in October
item.description: Food and non-alcoholic drinks also saw price increases for the second month running.

item.title: Tanzania adopts new tools in malaria fight
item.description: Improved nets, medicines, and vaccines offer hope but elimination remains distant.

item.title: Angola beat Ghana 2-0 in amputee World Cup opener
item.description: Ghana's Black Challenge now face Iraq in a must-win group game at the tournament in Mexico, their head coach has said.

item.title: Tanzania miners seek loan security for licences
item.description: Small-scale miners in Tanzania are struggling to access finance as banks do not recognise mining licences as loan security, hindering business growth.

item.title: Sudan school reopens after three-year war closure
item.description: Community efforts and local donations revive Sango Mixed Secondary School in South Darfur, now serving more than 115 students.

item.title: US basketball player arrested with 34kg cannabis in Lagos
item.description: Greene Da'monte Khiree was detained at the airport after abandoning luggage containing a potent strain of cannabis.

item.title: Raga leaders urge youth to return to school
item.description: Officials and traditional chiefs met to address low enrolment, which the students' association says leaves the county's future at risk.

item.title: NDC elects regional executives across Ghana
item.description: The governing party held elections supervised by the Electoral Commission to select new regional leaders for the next four years.

item.title: Vision FC tops Burundi's league table with 27 points from 12 matches
item.description: Vision FC has a goal difference of 21, while Muzinga FC sits three points behind in second place with 24 points from 12 games.

item.title: Ahmadiyya mission in Bondoukou urges justice as pillar of peace
item.description: At a symposium on Sunday, 15 November 2026, the local Islamic mission argued that fair treatment for all is essential to lasting peace in Ivory Coast.

item.title: Mali invests in school infrastructure
item.description: Education Minister Amadou Sy Savané announced significant funding for new classrooms and school facilities.

item.title: Mupetami wins Namibia sport journalist award for sixth time
item.description: Journalist Limba Mupetami of The New Era has been named sport journalist of the year at the Namibia Annual Sports Awards, her sixth win.

item.title: Ivory Coast can qualify for CAN 2027 this week
item.description: Cameroon, Senegal, Morocco and DR Congo also have a chance to book their places in the continental tournament during the fourth matchday of qualifying.

item.title: Vehicle crashes into home in N'Djaména, killing one
item.description: A car left the road in the capital's Kallatchou district on Sunday, hitting a house and leaving one dead and two seriously injured.

item.title: Opposition NDC says Zambia's Grow Zambia Agenda is failing in practice
item.description: National Democratic Congress president Saboi Imboela says the 2027 national budget does not show the agenda delivering results, and the government has asked the opposition.

item.title: US sends DR Congo list of agencies receiving over $400 million for Ebola
item.description: Washington has handed Kinshasa the names of the agencies that will receive its Ebola response funding, estimated at more than $400 million.

item.title: Emmaus expands in Libya through drug distribution deal
item.description: The American biopharmaceutical company has signed an exclusive distribution agreement with a Libyan pharmaceutical importer to grow its presence in the country.

item.title: Uganda army passes out platoon commanders
item.description: Officers completed intensive leadership and command training at two military schools.

item.title: Fecafoot absent from Jean Manga Onguéné's funeral in Yaoundé
item.description: The football federation did not attend the ceremonies held from Friday 13 to Saturday 14 November 2026 for one of the sport's pioneers.

item.title: Gambian journalists fault electoral commission over candidate asset scrutiny
item.description: Nine presidential candidates have been cleared for the 5 December vote, but the electoral commission has not opened their asset declarations to public review.

item.title: PAC asks President Mutharika for a meeting
item.description: The Public Affairs Committee has written to the president seeking an audience, and says it is still waiting for a date.

item.title: Wagner mercenaries fail to dislodge rebels in Kwango
item.description: Russian Wagner Group fighters returned to Bangui without removing armed elements suspected of being former UPC fighters from the Kwango area.

item.title: Six armed men rob Ugandan petrol station of Shs 14m
item.description: The robbers used a chemical substance to incapacitate four workers before stealing cash, a laptop, and a CCTV device from the Stabex station in Lamwo.

item.title: Malawi trail Egypt and Angola in Afcon qualifiers
item.description: Angola's victory over South Sudan leaves Malawi four points behind Group B leaders.

item.title: Kenya probes looting of refugee offices in Dadaab
item.description: Government offices were vandalized and property looted following protests by Somali refugees.

item.title: Rwanda and DRC put rival candidates forward for OIF Secretary General
item.description: The contest for the francophone body's top post is being held at its 20th summit in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, while the two countries remain in conflict over eastern DRC.

item.title: Fire contained at Mavoko garment factory
item.description: Property worth millions of shillings was destroyed in a late Sunday night blaze along the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway.

item.title: Burkina Faso energy access hits 36% in 2025
item.description: National energy report shows primary energy supply up 6.61% and final consumption up 8.3% between 2024 and 2025.

item.title: South Sudan Supreme Court disposes of 317 cases
item.description: The court handled 317 cases in 15 months, but faces funding and staffing challenges.

item.title: Ghana cybersecurity losses hit GHS209.7 million
item.description: Financial losses from cyber incidents between January and September 2026 far exceeded the total for 2025, raising concerns.

item.title: ZRA says fake export claims drain treasury
item.description: The Zambia Revenue Authority paid K25 billion in VAT refunds last year, with fraudulent claims costing the treasury.

item.title: Millennium bim donates food to Casa do Gaiato in Boane
item.description: The bank's donation supports a Maputo province institution that serves more than 300 meals every day to children, young people and staff.

item.title: Ghana takes in 42.5 to 62 tonnes of mercury a year through illicit routes
item.description: Gold miners in four regions handle the toxic metal daily, and stakeholders say it is reaching water supplies and the food chain.

item.title: South Sudan's Cairo embassy opens registration for voluntary return
item.description: The government has approved more than 26.5 million US dollars to bring home about 20,000 vulnerable citizens from Egypt.

item.title: IMF says Ghana's reforms are bearing fruit with stronger growth
item.description: The IMF says the economy grew 6% last year and inflation has fallen to single digits, after a difficult period of policy changes.

item.title: DR Congo provinces reject separatism
item.description: Representatives from Tshopo, Bas-Uele, Haut-Uele, and Ituri reaffirmed national unity at a meeting in Kisangani.

item.title: Malawi hospital gets power after social media outcry
item.description: Local Government Minister Ben Phiri confirmed electricity was restored to Makanjira Rural Hospital within 48 hours.

item.title: Eritrea and Ethiopia trade drone and artillery strikes
item.description: Fighting near the disputed town of Badme has intensified, driving civilians from their homes.

item.title: Mondlane treason trial begins Tuesday
item.description: Supreme Court sets aside seats for press and civil society in the treason trial of opposition leader Venâncio Mondlane.

item.title: Mozambique signs $500 million development financing deal with UAE fund
item.description: The Abu Dhabi Fund for Development will finance priority projects that Mozambique's government identifies, and Mozambique becomes its 109th partner country.

item.title: DBN targets US$750m in climate finance by 2029
item.description: The Development Bank of Namibia aims to raise the money through partnerships with development lenders and private investors, against a national climate investment need.

item.title: Ismaëlle Sanda goes to Tashkent to represent Madagascar in Our Generation 2026
item.description: The young singer will perform a song written for the contest in the international final on 20 November.

item.title: Frédéric Rabekoto wins Madagascar rally title in Moramanga
item.description: Rabekoto takes the 46th Grand Rallye de Madagascar by Orange, his first national rally championship, after a close duel with Olivier Ramiandrisoa.

item.title: Madagascar's Catholic bishops call for inclusive national consultation
item.description: In a statement after their November session, the bishops warned that decisions imposed in advance would not reflect the voice of the people.

item.title: Eswatini PM says no one is above the law, foreign firms included
item.description: Prime Minister Russell Mmiso Dlamini says businesses operating illegally on Swazi Nation Land must obey the law or face consequences.

item.title: Analyst says Nigeria is already a one-man state, not a one-party state
item.description: The ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) now controls 31 of Nigeria's 36 states, up from 21 at the end of the 2023 election cycle.

item.title: Soldiers accused of aiding cigarette smugglers
item.description: Vendors claim some Eswatini soldiers accept bribes to allow illegal tobacco into the country from Mozambique.

item.title: Eswatini minister urges chiefs to turn indigenous economies into jobs
item.description: S'khumbuzo Dlamini told the African Traditional Leaders Forum in Addis Ababa that informal traditional activities should become formal industries.

item.title: Central African Republic negotiates new fuel deal with Russia
item.description: Officials have not disclosed how much fuel Russia would sell, at what price, or through which channel it would be delivered.

item.title: Rwanda votes for UN draft on mercenaries
item.description: A UN committee approved the Cuban-led text on November 13, with 117 votes in favour, 54 against and seven abstentions.

item.title: Austrian investor disputes Gambian partners over Bitcoin Towers
item.description: DI Manuel Stofleth-Mitterer claims financial impropriety and intimidation in projects including Bitcoin Towers, Kasumai Real Estate, MASThave Real Estate, and Tujereng Housing.

item.title: Barrow launches 7.7km road widening project in Greater Banjul
item.description: President Adama Barrow laid the foundation stone for the project and inaugurated the newly completed Sukuta-Jabang Road on Sunday.

item.title: Castel Malawi pauses plan to cut 100 jobs for three weeks
item.description: The brewer, which says a tough trading climate is hurting its operations, agreed with its union to suspend the retrenchments while talks with government take place.

item.title: Abidjan hosts African oil producers' executive council meeting
item.description: Ivory Coast is hosting the 29th ordinary meeting of the Executive Council of the African Petroleum Producers' Organization (APPO) until Monday, 16 November.

item.title: Trindade beats Inter de Bombom on penalties to reach STP Cup final
item.description: Trindade Futebol Clube won the shootout 4-3 after a goalless 90 minutes and will face 1.º de Maio da Ilha do Príncipe for the trophy.

item.title: Darboe's UDP gains three alliance partners before December 5 vote
item.description: The Gambia First Coalition, led by the United Democratic Party, was sealed at a Manjai ceremony attended by senior members and journalists.

item.title: Gambia rural youth demand voice beyond ballot
item.description: Young Gambians in farming communities want their concerns addressed by leaders, not just during elections.

item.title: Guinea seeks Senegal's local development model
item.description: A Guinean delegation visits Senegal this week to learn from its community development program.

item.title: EYEOP gets siSwati name Litsafa Lensha
item.description: The Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project adopted a new name and logo to boost youth economic opportunities.

item.title: Lutundula threatens DR Congo suspension from OIF if Mushikiwabo is re-elected
item.description: Former foreign minister Christophe Lutundula says Kinshasa could suspend its participation in the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) if Kigali keeps Louise.

item.title: ANC factions clash over election results and GNU
item.description: Divisions within the ANC deepen as some members blame the DA partnership for poor local election results and seek to reconfigure the government of national unity.

item.title: Le Faso Digital closes second edition with awards
item.description: The event celebrated laureates and partners, with a virtual platform remaining open until 2028.

item.title: Abba Ibrahim wins Niamey centennial Kokowa competition
item.description: The national champion defeated his older brother in the final match of the traditional wrestling event.

item.title: Niger records 7,116 road accidents in 2025, with 1,245 killed
item.description: Transport Minister Colonel Major Abdourahamane Amadou announced the figures ahead of the 15th African Road Safety Day, and the government has declared 2026 the year of road.

item.title: EU project boosts goat farming in Burkina Faso's Koulsé region
item.description: A European Union-funded initiative provides livestock and training to displaced families, enabling income generation.

item.title: South Africa struggles to police online betting sites
item.description: Gross gambling revenue rose 13.4% to R84.5-billion in the 2025/26 financial year, with betting taking 74% of it.

item.title: Chitambala penalties send Zambia U-23 into next round
item.description: Zambia overturned a 1-0 first-leg defeat to Burkina Faso, winning the shootout 3-2 after a 1-1 aggregate draw in Lusaka.

item.title: Achi seeks parliamentary models abroad
item.description: Ivory Coast's National Assembly president Patrick Achi visited the UK, Paris, and met Canadian senators to modernize legislative processes.

item.title: Congo Independant columnist warns of verbal excess in DR Congo
item.description: In an opinion column, the writer argues that a flood of public commentary is outpacing analysis and results, and links it to the candidacy of Juliana Amato Lumumba to the OIF.

item.title: Dom Victor Luís Quematcha installed as Bishop of Bissau
item.description: The new Catholic bishop used his first speech to urge dialogue, accountability and peace during what he called a decisive moment for the country.

item.title: Gas tankers Derna and Al-Tahadi boost Libyan supplies
item.description: Gas deliveries have resumed to restock company depots as congestion begins to ease, according to Brega Petroleum Marketing Company.

item.title: Libya's Health Ministry reports girl's death from toxic wild mushrooms
item.description: 17-year-old Maryam Jassim Saeed died after eating poisonous wild mushrooms, the ministry said, with several other patients treated at Al-Bayda Medical Center.

item.title: Doune Pathé Mbengue unveils plan to reshape Senegal's port network
item.description: The Port Autonome de Dakar plans to reconfigure the Dakar port, convert Ndayane into a multi-terminal platform and link ports from Saint-Louis to Ziguinchor.

item.title: Algeria launches electronic land document certification
item.description: The national land directorate's digital portal now issues legally recognized electronic land documents.

item.title: Egypt and Kuwait sign agreements at joint committee
item.description: The 14th session of the Egyptian-Kuwaiti Joint Committee ended with several agreements and memoranda of understanding signed in Kuwait on Sunday.

item.title: Zotus Group clears international money-laundering checks for Kalahari City
item.description: The Botswana Investment and Trade Centre says the developer's accreditation is not yet final project approval.

item.title: New bishop shares pastoral vision for Sarh diocese
item.description: Monseigneur Jean Miguina aims for an engaged Church focused on education, poverty, and peace.
